text:
Good evening. It is Saturday night, and here is your political news briefing.

First, the news from home.

Story one. A national debate has emerged over Ghana's move to join the BRICS bloc. Graphic Online reports that the founder and leader of the All People’s Congress, Hassan Ayariga, has questioned Cabinet's authority to pursue membership without parliamentary scrutiny and public consultation, while MyJoyOnline reports that Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa defended the bid, arguing that even the United States deals with Russia in pursuit of its national interests.

Story two. The appointment of Emelia Affi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission continues to generate political friction. According to MyJoyOnline, Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa acknowledged that the public optics surrounding her appointment are not good, while 3News reports that political commentator Senyo Hosi called for her resignation and former deputy minister Felix Kwakye Ofosu urged critics to give her a chance to prove herself.

Story three. Former Vice President and New Patriotic Party flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia says the party has resolved its internal wrangling, according to MyJoyOnline. He urged party members at constituency and polling station levels to remain formidable, while The Ghana Report notes that Member of Parliament Sammi Awuku also cautioned members against internal divisions as the party prepares for twenty twenty-eight.

Story four. Internal party contest preparations are picking up ahead of upcoming regional races. Both MyJoyOnline and Starr F M report that Michael Tetteh Kwetey has secured the number one spot on the ballot paper for the National Democratic Congress Greater Accra Regional Chairmanship election scheduled for November twenty twenty-six.

Now, around the world.

Story five. United States President Donald Trump has temporarily waived several sanctions on Moscow recently passed by Congress, sparking immediate international and bipartisan domestic criticism. The Guardian and Al Jazeera report that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the decision as a reward for Vladimir Putin that will embolden the Russian leader, while American lawmakers from both the Republican and Democratic parties warned the waiver undermines Ukraine.

Story six. Senegal’s former President Macky Sall has officially withdrawn from the race to become the next Secretary General of the United Nations, according to Africanews. His decision comes after an informal United Nations Security Council straw poll in which all seven candidates received at least one veto from a permanent member.

You can open Dad News and ask for more about any story by its number.
